record.original_question: Among all connected graphs on n vertices, does the lollipop graph P_{n-3} · K_4 minimize the l1-norm of the principal eigenvector?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 24 (Rücker-Rücker-Gutman [133]). Among all connected graphs on n vertices, the graph P_{n−3} · K_4 minimizes l1-norm ||x||_1 of principal eigenvectors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A(G)$. By the Perron–Frobenius theorem, $A(G)$ has a unique (up to positive scaling) positive unit eigenvector $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)$ associated with its largest eigenvalue; this $x$ is called the principal eigenvector of $G$. Normalize $x$ so that $\|x\|_2 = 1$ (Euclidean unit norm), and define the $\ell_1$-norm of the principal eigenvector by $\|x\|_1 = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i$.

For $n \ge 7$, let $P_{n-3}\cdot K_4$ denote the lollipop graph obtained from a complete graph $K_4$ and a path $P_{n-3}$ on $n-3$ vertices by identifying one endpoint of the path with a single vertex of $K_4$ (so the resulting graph has $n$ vertices and is connected).

Prove or disprove: among all connected graphs on $n$ vertices, the lollipop graph $P_{n-3}\cdot K_4$ uniquely minimizes the $\ell_1$-norm $\|x\|_1$ of its principal eigenvector.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related extremal-eigenvector problems (e.g., the Cioabă–Gregory principal ratio conjecture, resolved by Tait–Tobin), but no source reports a resolution of the specific Rücker–Rücker–Gutman conjecture that the lollipop $P_{n-3}\cdot K_4$ minimizes the $\ell_1$-norm of the principal eigenvector among connected $n$-vertex graphs. It appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on graph eigenvalues; lists conjectures including those by Rücker–Rücker–Gutman about principal eigenvectors.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture appears in surveys of open spectral graph theory problems and is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting the Maximum Principal Ratio of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the related Cioabă–Gregory principal-ratio conjecture proved by Tait and Tobin; distinct from the l1-norm minimization conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct extremal eigenvector problems have been studied; no result resolves the l1-norm minimization conjecture for P_{n-3}·K_4.
